items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Then, then we brought in, uh, uh, Joe Marcella, and, uh, made up a lot of groups

ctx.x: I see. Yeah. Well, this, combining good jazz with commercial appeal, I think it deserves a great deal of attention. And you're being manager of the band, give you a little time to think about some of these things.

I'll say so. Well, the evolution of jazz in New York, you know, covers a big field. And when I joined Victor, as a manager of autism repertoire in 1935, my job then was to, to sort of lean over backward, to see if the, those people who were jazz minded, couldn't get more product. And it was then that I began bringing in bands in the Victor, for instance, Adrian Malini came in with a group, and he was playing at the Hickory House, not the Hickory House, but the, this, the present hotel. He had a little joint down…
